claims.statement: SummarizationMiddleware retains raw messages and reconstructs model-visible history from a summary event followed by the retained suffix; each event records its cutoff, cutoff message ID, summary, optional archive path, and creation index, and resolves the ID before falling back to the numeric cutoff when earlier state messages have been removed.

Context-overflow recovery sends at most one strictly smaller retry, rejects known over-budget reduced requests before calling the provider, and raises a terminal ContextOverflowError after recovery is exhausted.

SummarizationToolMiddleware exposes compact_conversation for explicit compaction, reuses a configured SummarizationMiddleware, shares its summary-event and session-id state with automatic compaction, and admits a call only when a trigger clause reaches about half of its configured threshold.

The SDK archive helpers convert backend read/write failures into a None path, so manual compact_conversation records a successful but non-recoverable summary event; a summary-generation failure or offload exception that escapes the helper instead returns a correlated error ToolMessage without writing summarization-event or session-ID state.

dcode server-owned offload locks a registered idle or errored thread, rejects pending graph work, verifies the checkpoint has not advanced after summarization, and commits only allowlisted summary-event, session-ID, and cost channels rather than conversation messages.

dcode reserves a forced-offload summary event before writing its deferred archive; if the archive append fails it keeps the committed in-context summary without a path, while a failed archive-link write rolls back the append only when readback confirms the path is absent.

Local dcode conversation archives normally live in a hardened conversation_history directory under DEEPAGENTS_HOME, fall back to hardened temporary storage marked ephemeral when persistent storage is unavailable, and are swept according to history.retention_days without propagating cleanup failures.

Idle dcode compaction is opt-in through history.idle_compaction_tokens and is scheduled at most once per thread and prompt-cache window only in the final 20% of the cache window capped at 120 seconds, with exact context usage, a remote agent, and a quiescent UI.

ManagedMemoryGuardMiddleware intercepts mutations of configured guarded memory files, restores a changed marker-delimited managed block while preserving other edits where possible, returns an error if restoration fails, and rejects destructive deletion of protected or unreadable existing files before the tool runs.

The dcode offload HTTP boundary discards request-supplied model settings and derives the offload model and parameters from the target checkpoint; threads without checkpointed model metadata use the startup summarizer.

For an offload state-write failure, dcode rolls back drained cost records only when the checkpoint is confirmed unchanged; if the checkpoint advanced or cannot be read back, it keeps records claimed and reports an indeterminate outcome to avoid double charging.

dcode handoff summarizes a source thread without writing a summary event to that source, persists only its cost channels there, and names recovery snapshots by source-thread ownership so deletion cleanup can remove them.
Managed-memory reads and restoration writes use no-follow file operations, so a guarded-file symlink replacement causes a visible restoration failure rather than overwriting the symlink target.

dcode normalizes provider truncation metadata and turns an empty truncated final reply into ModelOutputTruncatedError so the model node fails instead of checkpointing a silent empty success; task-subagent failures become error ToolMessages while partial subagent replies retain content with a warning.

dcode anchors a summary event's numeric cutoff to its retained-boundary message ID and shifts its creation index by the same amount, allowing index-only consumers to agree after earlier checkpoint messages were removed.

Goal control and goal-state messages are framework-owned HumanMessages marked by lc_source: they remain model-visible in normal turn order but are excluded from user-facing transcript, title, and derived-conversation projections; oversized goal state is replaced with bounded guidance that prevents the model from acting on it.

After a valid unprocessed summarization cutoff, LocalContextMiddleware refreshes detected environment context and appends a model-only, untrusted-data message only when its fingerprint changed; it records the cutoff even when detection yields no output.

A forced dcode offload plan performs summary generation without archive I/O, and the archive write path snapshots prior content and refuses to overwrite an existing archive after a backend-read error.

CLIContextSchema normalizes the per-run context at the local/RemoteGraph boundary: local executions receive the registered dataclass while API executions may supply a dict; malformed containers are replaced with empty values, booleans are rejected as context limits, and malformed auto-approval values fail closed.

A declarative SDK subagent is isolated by default and sees only its delegated task; experimental fork mode instead passes the parent's effective summarized history plus a task preamble, and refuses nested task delegation.

Forked subagents inherit the parent prompt-producing middleware and skills rather than accepting their own skills, while their authored instructions are placed in the task message to preserve the inherited system-prompt prefix; compiled forks do not receive private state channels.

dcode enables fork mode for its generated general-purpose subagent when FORKED_SUBAGENTS is truthy, and injects its filesystem-tool allowlist into each custom subagent so delegated tools cannot bypass the parent restriction.

The external editor prepares a temporary UTF-8 Markdown draft and returns normalized edited text without directly mutating agent state; nonzero exit or blank text normally returns None, and cleanup errors are suppressed.

dcode completion derives its command tree from the argparse parser and filters generated completion words through a shell-safe allowlist, keeping bash, zsh, and fish scripts aligned with the real CLI without emitting unsafe candidates.
